subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw permanently own a cooperative `fs.glob`-compatible walker for `bootstrap-extra-files` and allow event-loop turns between `agent:bootstrap` hook handlers to protect gateway responsiveness?
rationale: The benchmark supports the responsiveness objective, but exact glob compatibility and hook-dispatch atomicity are durable core behavior choices that cannot be resolved safely by a mechanical patch adjustment alone.

options.title: Approve the internal contract
options.body: Accept the yielding walker and scheduled bootstrap dispatch as the canonical core behavior after owner review of the stated parity and ordering boundary.

options.title: Keep Node glob semantics
options.body: Retain the existing glob implementation and pursue responsiveness through narrower scheduling or runtime-level changes that do not reimplement glob behavior.

options.title: Split the proposal
options.body: Land only independently approved async read or diagnostic work and defer glob replacement and hook scheduling to separate owner-reviewed changes.

recommendation.title: Approve the internal contract
recommendation.body: Accept the yielding walker and scheduled bootstrap dispatch as the canonical core behavior after owner review of the stated parity and ordering boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Explicitly brought into the PR discussion and the best available routing signal for the core behavior decision.
